    AI Overview
    President Trump fired Attorney General Pam Bondi on April 2, 2026, after a 14-month tenure, driven by frustration over her handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files and failure to prosecute political opponents
    . Her, reported, "fumbling" of the files and inability to manage the scandal created political liability. 
    Key reasons for her ouster included: 
    • Epstein Files Handling: Bondi faced intense criticism for her management of the Epstein files, including failed promises to release all documents and missteps in releasing sensitive victim information.
    • Lack of Political Prosecutions: Trump complained that she failed to aggressively investigate or prosecute his political enemies.
    • Damaged Credibility: Her actions on the Epstein case—including a false claim that a "client list" was on her desk—led to loss of confidence, even from Republican allies.
    • Rising Internal Criticism: She was criticized by White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles for her performance. 
    Following her firing, Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche was expected to become the acting attorney general.

    AI Overview
    As of March 2026, Pam Bondi is the
    U.S. Attorney General, confirmed following her role as a key ally to Donald Trump, lobbyist, and former Florida Attorney General (2011–2019). She has focused on anti-human trafficking efforts, defending Trump in impeachment proceedings, litigating conservative policies with the America First Policy Institute, and supporting 2020 election challenges. 
    Key actions and roles include: 
    • U.S. Attorney General (2025–Present): Confirmed to the position, she has been involved in overseeing prosecutions of political adversaries and restructuring DOJ staff.
    • Florida Attorney General (2011–2019): Served as Florida’s first female Attorney General, focusing on cracking down on "pill mills" and combating human trafficking.
    • Trump Ally and Defense:
      Served on President Trump’s legal defense team during his first impeachment trial and worked as a special advisor.
    • Lobbyist and Legal Counsel: Worked for Ballard Partners, representing various corporate and foreign interests, including the Qatari government.
    • America First Policy Institute (AFPI): Led litigation efforts at the pro-Trump think tank, targeting voting rights and other policies.
    • Election Challenges: Was involved in questioning the 2020 election results, according to Common Cause. 
    Bondi is a former prosecutor and native of Tampa, Florida.

CNN reports that Environmental Protection Agency administrator Lee Zeldin is up for consideration as Bondi’s replacement. In a Truth Social Post on Thursday afternoon Trump said, “Pam Bondi is a Great American Patriot and a loyal friend, who faithfully served as my Attorney General over the past year.
